reference_meta.title: Līlāvatī of Bhāskara II (with Sanskrit anvaya and Hindi commentary)

reference_meta.coverage_note: Colebrooke translates the verse and Bhāskara's statement/solution; he has no equivalent of the Sanskrit anvaya or the modern Hindi explanation. Colebrooke printed the fractions stacked; all four archive.org OCRs of the 1817 book garble them (e.g. 'i', '%^', 'y'), so each is marked '[fraction illegible in OCR]' rather than supplied (true values per the page: 1/8; 7/8; 80/7 and 48/7; 40/7). OCR letter errors corrected: 'M&nasa' -> 'Mánasa' (as in https://archive.org/download/1817-henry-colebrooke-algebra-with-arithmetic-and-mensuration-from-the-sanskrit-of-br/1817-HCOLEBROOKE_Algebra_with_Arithmetic_and_Mensuration_from_the_Sanskrit_of_Brahmagupta_and_Bhaskara_djvu.txt), 'coefiicient' -> 'coefficient'; footnote markers dropped. No neighbouring examples included (they carry further garbled fractions).
reference_meta.page_content: Example verse (flock of geese; ten times the square root to the Mānasa lake, an eighth to the sthalapadminī forest, three pairs remain), Sanskrit anvaya, Hindi artha, Sanskrit nyāsa (statement and working: 7/8, 48/7, 80/7, 40/7, 1600/49, 1936/49, 44/7, 144), and the start of a Hindi worked explanation (phailāv) cut off at page foot. The reference covers the verse, anvaya, artha and nyāsa (~60% of the page); the Hindi phailāv (~40%) has no reference beyond the matching steps in Colebrooke's solution.
reference_meta.source: H. T. Colebrooke, Algebra, with Arithmetic and Mensuration, from the Sanscrit of Brahmegupta and Bháscara, London: John Murray 1817, Líláwatí ch. III sect. V §66 (p. 30)
